sections.name: supportedOutcome
sections.title: Works out project outcome from facts
sections.what: Keeps only facts that passed strict checks, then assigns one of four labels based on cancellation, completion or operational wording, construction or planning wording, or otherwise leaves it unassessed.
sections.why: The header says the Yard's status alone is not evidence, so only admitted facts count.
sections.watch_out: The check for In progress has no negation test, so a status such as no longer planned still returns In progress.

summary: Works out a project's outcome label (Delivered, In progress, Cautionary or Unassessed) from facts that have passed strict checks.
purpose: Gives a project a simple status label based only on verified evidence.
why: The header says the Yard's status and forecast amounts are not verified outcome evidence, so they are not used on their own.
how: 1. Keeps only facts that are verified, relevant, from a direct source, matched to the project and supported. 2. If the status text says cancelled, canceled, suspended or abandoned, returns Cautionary. 3. If there is a completion fact, or status text says commercial operation, entered service or operational, returns Delivered. 4. If the status text says under construction, in construction, planning or planned, returns In progress. 5. Otherwise returns Unassessed.
inputs: A list of research facts, each with its honesty, relevance, assessment and field path.
risks: Word matching is simple, so unusual wording can give the wrong label. Negation words are checked only for the first two labels, not for In progress.
debug: Look at the facts passed in and the status text they contain. A fact that fails any single gate is ignored, which often leaves the label at Unassessed.
